remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Thought provoking post by Dwarkesh. In general - as AI gets more powerful - we should expect on the margin that inference goes toward the most economically useful task, and everything else gets priced out. 

This in theory in a very scarce environment would cause the cost of inference to skyrocket because those tasks would be far more valuable than today. 

But I don’t think it plays out in the way that’s laid out just simply due to market forces competing for inference demand as a way of continuing to drive down prices until capacity can catch up.

There are too many model providers and infra players that want these workloads to cause the effect that’s proposed here. But will see!
remarks.translation: 德瓦凯什的这篇帖子引人深思。总体而言——随着人工智能日益强大——我们应当预期，推理能力会逐渐向最具经济价值的任务倾斜，其他用途则会被价格挤出市场。理论上，在资源极度稀缺的环境下，这会导致推理成本飙升，因为这些任务的价值将远超当前水平。但我认为，实际情况不会完全按照这种设想发展，原因很简单：市场力量会争夺推理需求，持续压低价格，直到算力供应跟上。有太多模型供应商和基础设施参与者渴望承接这些工作负载，从而抵消这里提出的效应。不过，拭目以待吧！

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
AI has been great for my productivity, but I’m starting to recognize three dark patterns:

1. Becoming too lazy to read anything

It's too easy to just read AI summaries over the original piece or let agents go wild changing my files without reviewing what they did.

2. Getting distracted by agents while I’m out

It’s too easy to open ChatGPT or Claude on my phone while I’m out to give feedback my agents and feel “productive,” even when I’m supposed to be watching my kids or doing literally anything else.

3. Preferring to talk to the agent vs. a human

This is a new pattern with ChatGPT Voice, I sometimes find myself preferring to brainstorm with the agent instead of the actual human in the room.
remarks.translation:
人工智能极大地提升了我的工作效率，但我开始注意到三种不良模式：  
1. 变得过于懒惰，不愿阅读任何内容  
直接看AI摘要而非原文，或任由代理随意修改文件而不检查其操作，实在太容易了。  
2. 外出时被代理分散注意力  
在外出时，本该照看孩子或做其他事情，却轻易打开手机上的ChatGPT或Claude给代理反馈，还觉得自己“很高效”。  
3. 更倾向于与代理而非真人交流  
这是ChatGPT语音功能带来的新模式，我有时发现自己宁愿与代理头脑风暴，也不愿与房间里的真人交流。

remarks.role: ceo every
remarks.text:
incredibly good write up 

bad actors will obviously try to use models to do stuff like this on purpose in the future. 

on the bright side:

- OpenAI’s safety classifiers were turned off, the model was explicitly directed to do exploits
- HG’s AI actually surfaced the attack automatically (though not with a high enough criticality) 

Will obviously require any company dealing with sensitive customer data to have automated agentic defense systems, massive opportunity and seems effective
remarks.translation:
非常出色的分析。未来，恶意行为者显然会故意利用模型进行此类操作。积极的一面是：  
- OpenAI 的安全分类器被关闭，模型被明确指示进行漏洞利用  
- HG 的 AI 实际上自动发现了这次攻击（尽管关键性评级不够高）  
显然，任何处理敏感客户数据的公司都需要配备自动化的智能防御系统，这既是巨大的机遇，也似乎非常有效。

remarks.name: Aditya Agarwal
remarks.role: General Partner SouthPkCommons, Co-Founder Bevel_Health
remarks.text:
Some observations from our Demo Faire yesterday:

1/ There is a tremendous amount of interest from the larger investor community for frontier technology. Robots. Drones. Semiconductors. Bring it all. 

2/ The interest in Frontier Tech is legitimately Based. People want 🇺🇸 to win.

3/ The bar for "great" in software has gone up a lot. If you are building something that resembles vertical SaaS or agent-for-X, then you have to show something truly different in terms of vision or on a bonkers ramp.

4/ You should only do early stage investing if you love building the future. That is the real joy of it. It was so cool to see everyone deeply engaging with our founders about what they were building (as opposed to simply asking for up and to the right graphs).

5/ Silicon Valley does best when we understand that it takes a village to build something special for many decades.
remarks.translation: 昨日演示展的一些观察：1/ 大型投资群体对前沿科技的兴趣极为浓厚。机器人、无人机、半导体，全盘接收。2/ 对前沿科技的兴趣确实根基深厚。人们希望🇺🇸赢得胜利。3/ 软件领域"卓越"的标准已大幅提升。若你在构建类似垂直SaaS或X领域智能体的产品，就必须在愿景层面展现真正差异，或呈现爆发式增长曲线。4/ 唯有热爱构建未来，才应从事早期投资。这才是真正的乐趣所在。看到众人与创始人深入探讨他们正在创造的事物（而非仅索取持续增长的图表），实在令人振奋。5/ 当硅谷领悟到需要整个生态体系数十年持续耕耘才能铸就非凡时，便是其最佳状态。

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
The openai agent sandbox escape actually has very real implications for the diffusion of AI in the enterprise. The incident showed the power and capability of agents, and the need to harden systems and environments to prepare for agents.

There are tons of measures that enterprises must take to ensure that agents are only able to operate on the data they give it, the ability to have audit trails and governance of what agents can do, figure out what systems should remain deterministic vs. nondeterministic, get access controls under control, have the ability to quickly block and defend if an agent goes rogue, and much more.

Even in the happy path case with a good actor, if you give an agent a task like "find all of our most important IP on project Maven" it will gladly go out and execute that work -no matter how long- and find any resource relevant to the task. It might run into data with out of date access controls or reveal something that you shouldn't know about. Then, in the non-happy path case with a malicious actor the risk is clearly far worse.

In theory, you had to worry about this for people as well, but with AI the risks are inherently amplified. Agents will happily spend any amount of time on a task, don’t actually face any *real* risks by going rogue, and don’t have the inherent judgment (yet) that a person does that a task might make no sense. This means you need an all new way of managing data and protecting environments.

This obviously creates a huge opportunity for the startup and security ecosystems because there will be many different approaches to how we lock down agents or at least the underlying systems they work with. It should update everyone’s timelines on diffusion, though, as it also means that enterprises will have another step of work they have to go through for agents to handle more autonomous work.
remarks.translation: OpenAI 智能体沙箱逃逸事件，对企业级 AI 的普及有着非常现实的影响。这一事件展示了智能体的强大能力，也凸显了加固系统和环境以迎接智能体时代的必要性。企业必须采取大量措施，确保智能体只能操作其被授权的数据，建立审计追踪和治理机制来管控智能体的行为，明确哪些系统应保持确定性、哪些可接受非确定性，强化访问控制，并具备在智能体失控时快速阻断和防御的能力，等等。即使在正常场景下，面对一个善意的使用者，如果你给智能体下达一个任务，比如“找出我们在 Maven 项目上所有最重要的知识产权”，它会毫不犹豫地去执行——无论耗时多久——并找到所有相关资源。它可能会接触到访问控制已过时的数据，或揭示出你不该知晓的信息。而在非正常场景下，面对恶意行为者，风险显然要严重得多。理论上，这类风险对人类同样需要防范，但 AI 会从根本上放大这些风险。智能体会不计时间地投入任务，失控时并不面临任何*真实*风险，且（目前）不具备人类那种判断任务是否合理的直觉。这意味着，你需要一套全新的数据管理和环境保护方式。这显然为初创企业和安全生态系统创造了巨大机遇，因为如何锁定智能体，或至少锁定其运行的底层系统，将涌现出多种不同的方法。不过，这也应促使大家重新调整对 AI 普及时间表的预期，因为这也意味着，企业要让智能体处理更自主的工作，还需经历一个额外的准备阶段。

remarks.text:
First kid teaches you unconditional love. 

Second kid teaches you unbridled joy. 

As AGI (digital & physical) comes close, having close family and friends is going to be the most important (only?) human connection we have. So if you are on the fence, let this be a vote in the yes direction!

Don’t get me wrong having kids is really hard and one of life’s only irreversible choices - the highs are really high and the lows well sometimes can be very low (mostly temporary though). 

But oh my, it’s such a privilege to have these two and I honestly wouldn’t trade it for anything else!
remarks.translation: 第一个孩子教会你无条件的爱，第二个孩子教会你纯粹的快乐。随着通用人工智能（数字与实体形态）日益临近，拥有亲密的家人和朋友将成为我们最重要（甚至唯一？）的人类联结。所以如果你还在犹豫，请把这当作投给"要孩子"的一票！别误会，养育孩子确实非常艰难，也是人生中为数不多的不可逆选择——快乐时极尽欢愉，低谷时也可能跌入深渊（不过大多都是暂时的）。但天哪，能拥有这两个小家伙是何等幸运，说实话，让我拿任何东西来换我都不愿意！

podcasts.title: 第90集：人工智能先驱尤尔根·施密德胡伯谈当今AI现状
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today
podcasts.excerpt: 尤尔根·施密德胡伯博士，这位享誉全球的科学家与人工智能研究者，被公认为该领域的先驱之一。他通过其实验室的工作，孕育了当今Transformer架构、长短期记忆网络（LSTM）以及递归自我改进等关键理念。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件瓶颈；随着开源技术紧追封闭实验室的步伐，当前对AI数据中心的投资热潮即将迎来修正；而通往通用智能的路径，在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非依赖互联网数据。在结尾部分，他重新审视了主流AI安全论点，并描绘了一幅宏大愿景：自我复制的机器人社会终将殖民整个太阳系。 (0:00) 引言 (1:24) 超人类AI还有多远？ (2:27) ChatGPT为何未令他惊讶 (3:21) 递归自我改进之路 (9:01) AI会迎来爆发式飞跃吗…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. (0:00) Intro (1:24) How Close Is Superhuman AI? (2:27) Why ChatGPT Didn't Surprise Him (3:21) The Path to Recursive Self-Improvement (9:01) Will AI Takeoff…

podcasts.excerpt: DoorDash 不仅仅是一家配送公司。从创立之初，联合创始人 Andy Fang 和 Stanley Tang 就将其作为一家机器人与自动驾驶公司来运营。Andy 和 Stanley 与 Sarah Guo 一起探讨了自动驾驶技术和人工智能如何重塑消费习惯、商业和配送。他们谈到了 Ask DoorDash 的推出，这是一个自然语言界面，既能推动餐厅发现，也能促进更大额的杂货订单。他们还讨论了 Dot，这是他们自主研发的自动驾驶配送机器人，已在凤凰城运营超过两年，并展示了他们在自动驾驶技术中面临并解决的运营和硬件挑战。Andy 和 Stanley 还谈到了自动驾驶配送中的“首尾 100 英尺问题”，为什么多模式策略是成功的关键，如何扩展自动驾驶和运营规模，以及为什么他们相信未来 DoorDash 需要更多而非更少的 Dasher。立即注册…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: DoorDash is not just a delivery company. From its inception, co-founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang operated it as a robotics and autonomy company. Andy and Stanley join Sarah Guo to explain how autonomous tech and AI are reshaping consumer habits, commerce, and delivery. Andy and Stanley talk about the rollout of Ask DoorDash, a natural-language interface that’s driving both restaurant discovery and larger grocery orders. They also discuss Dot, their in-house autonomous delivery robot that has operated in Phoenix for over two years, and how it highlights the operational and hardware challenges they have faced and solved in autonomous tech. Andy and Stanley also speak about the “first and last 100 feet problem” in autonomous delivery, why multimodal strategies are the key to success, scaling autonomy and operations, and why they believe that more Dashers, not fewer, are the future of DoorDash.  Sign u…
